problem: Deleting .agent/goal.json after an unmet block lets the session stop after one no-goal prompt, with no warning or gap record, and committed work with no upstream is never prompted.

note: Committed work in a repository with no upstream and no origin default branch is still not detected as changed; there is no reliable reference point.

problem: Any added test function anywhere licenses unlimited runtime prose growth, and against main the branch's existing test changes license growth with no new test.

note: Evidence is proportionate (150 words per added test or trial record) but not semantically tied to the new text; blind review remains the check on relevance.

problem: A finding is accepted as fixed and proven with an unrelated existing test and another finding's mutation, and addressed with note '.'.

problem: Here-strings, busybox/fish shells, interpreter system calls and variable command names bypass the guard, and some discard forms are not refused.
reproduction: bash <<< 'git push -f', busybox sh -c, fish -c, python3 -c os.system, $g push -f, git branch -f main HEAD~3, rm -rf ../repo, mv .git /tmp/x, git checkout -- '*.py' -> rc=0
note: Variable command names such as $g push -f stay allowed: refusing every variable command would block ordinary $EDITOR or $PYTHON use.

problem: The make -n dry run executes '+'-prefixed recipe lines, so checking a target has side effects.
reproduction: Makefile side: +touch SIDE_EFFECT; @false -> SIDE_EFFECT created
note: GNU make runs recipe lines prefixed with + even under -n by design; such targets declare that they must always run, so the dry run respects the project's own choice.

note: Squash merges leave no ancestry link, so detecting them needs content comparison that would be slow and unreliable; the branch-deletion rule still applies after squash merges.
